## PROPERTY INFORMATION
**Service Date:** 2026-05-14
**System Type:** Type 2 (Aerobic Treatment Unit)
**Maintenance Interval:** 12 months

## SYSTEM STATUS
This maintenance visit recorded a critical deficiency in pump operation. The effluent pump is running but drawing only 22.2% of its nameplate amperage, indicating no hydraulic load. This is a confirmed failure mode requiring immediate professional attention. All other measured components are in good condition, but the system cannot function safely or effectively until pump operation is restored.

## TANK MEASUREMENTS
| Measurement | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Scum Thickness | 3.0 in |
| Sludge Depth | 8.0 in |
| Total Fluid Depth | 48.0 in |
| Solids Content | 22.9% -- within normal range |

The liquid level is at the outlet. The effluent filter is in good condition with light soiling and was cleaned and reseated during this visit.

## PUMP OPERATION
| Measurement | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Measured Amp Draw | 1.6 A |
| Nameplate Rating | 7.2 A |
| Load Percentage | 22.2% FLA -- CRITICAL |

**CRITICAL - No Load.** The pump is running but drawing only 22.2% of its rated amperage. This indicates the pump is operating without hydraulic load. Possible causes include a dry run condition (no fluid reaching the pump), a broken or missing impeller, or a severed or disconnected discharge line. Continued operation without load creates a risk of motor overheating and damage.

The high water alarm tested functional. Electrical connections are sound.

## DISPERSAL FIELD
The dispersal field surface is dry with no evidence of breakout or ponding.

## WORK PERFORMED
- Cleaned and reseated the effluent filter
- Measured scum, sludge and total fluid depth
- Ran the effluent pump through a full cycle and measured amp draw
- Tested the high water alarm
- Walked the dispersal field and checked for surface breakout

## RECOMMENDATIONS

**Immediate Priority:**
- **Immediate professional attention required.** The effluent pump is operating at critical no-load condition. A qualified technician must examine the pump intake line, discharge line, and impeller to determine whether the pump is cavitating (running dry), the impeller is broken or missing, or the discharge line is severed or disconnected. Do not continue operating the system until the cause is identified and corrected. Continued no-load operation risks permanent motor damage.

**Secondary:**
- Once pump operation is restored, resume the 12-month maintenance interval.

## HOMEOWNER GUIDANCE

### About the Pump Failure
Your pump is running but not moving water. This is a serious condition because the motor is designed to be cooled by the fluid it pumps. Running without that cooling load causes the motor to overheat and can cause permanent damage within hours or days of continuous operation.

The problem is most likely one of three things: the pump intake is not getting water (dry run), the impeller inside the pump is broken, or the discharge line is disconnected or blocked. A technician will need to check all three. Do not delay -- the longer the pump runs in this condition, the greater the risk of having to replace it entirely.

### Tank Solids
This maintenance visit recorded solids at 22.9 percent of tank volume, which is within the normal range. Your tank is functioning normally from a biological standpoint. Continue to keep non-biodegradable material out of the system -- wipes, paper towels, cooking grease, and medications all interfere with the natural breakdown of solids.
